approach: Add an `athena.focus/1` record (`records/focus/focus-<n>.json`: n, at, text, set_by from git user.name) that `Athena::set_focus` writes and a new `athena focus [text]` command sets or prints. `Records` loads it and `athena status` shows the latest as a `focus` line. For the caps, add an optional `[priority_caps]` table (urgent=3, high=10) to the schema and athena.toml. In plan.rs add `Plan::build_capped(entries, history, caps, person_set) -> (Plan, Vec<PlanEntry>)`. It builds uncapped to get the plan order, then demotes excess urgent and high items on cloned entries, rebuilds, and returns the plan, with `Plan.demoted` filled in, together with the capped entries it built from. Person-set items are never demoted: they fill the cap first and only the other items drop. `Drain::prepare` (shared by `athena plan` and `drain`) calls it, runs `priority_violations` against the returned capped entries, and adds one `note_once` per demotion. Both `athena plan` and the `drain` report already print notes, so each demotion shows as one `note        demoted ...` line. Nothing under records/ is written by planning.

decisions.choice: Person-set items are never demoted. In each tier they are counted against the cap first. Only the other items fill the remaining slots, in plan order of the uncapped build, and the rest drop one tier. If person-set items alone exceed the cap, the tier holds more than the cap and nothing is demoted from them. `person_set` is therefore a plain list of job ids (any job with a priority record) and its order does not matter.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 2: the reading says a person's priority record always keeps its item at that tier, and criterion 3 needs the person-set urgent item among the 3 kept. 'Person-set first, most recent first' is honored as keep-first. Because none of them are ever demoted, recency has no effect, so the list is not ordered.

rejected.option: Rank person-set items first and keep only the first `cap` (the previous plan)
rejected.why: With cap+1 person-set items it demotes one, which breaks the rule that a person's record wins.
Contradicts criterion 3 and the rule that a person's record wins.

decisions.choice: One tier at most. An urgent item demoted to high counts toward the high cap (after person-set items, before native high items) and is never demoted again. Native non-person high items beyond the remaining slots drop to normal. Each demoted item therefore has exactly one `Demotion { id, from, to, cap }` and one note.
decisions.reason: The reading says demotion is one tier, and criterion 3 needs one demotion line per demoted item. This still lets a flood of urgent items press on the high cap.

rejected.option: Let a demoted urgent item be demoted again to normal in the same pass
rejected.why: Two tiers in one plan, and two lines for one item.

decisions.choice: `Plan::build_capped(entries, history, caps, person_set) -> (Plan, Vec<PlanEntry>)` returns the capped entries along with the plan, and `Drain::prepare` passes those to `priority_violations`. It wraps `build_with`. `build` and `build_with` are unchanged. `Plan` gains `demoted: Vec<Demotion>`, skipped in JSON when empty.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The order check must judge the order against the tiers the plan was built from. Checked against the originals, a demoted urgent item planned after an older native high item would give a false 'plan order contradicts priority' note (priority_violations, plan.rs:490, reads each entry's own priority). Demotion stays in memory because it works on clones, and Plan is pure data, so tests measure it directly.

rejected.option: Keep calling `priority_violations(&entries)` with the uncapped entries
rejected.why: Produces a false contradiction note for every demotion that lands behind an equal-tier item.

rejected.option: Add a tier or flag field to PlanEntry
rejected.why: PlanEntry is built by struct literal in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, which is not a deliverable, so it would stop compiling.
About 40 call sites in tests, reading.rs and drain.rs.

decisions.choice: Report demotions with one `note_once` per demotion in `Drain::prepare`, text `demoted <id> · <title> from <tier> to <tier>: over the <tier> cap of <n>`. `display::plan` gets no separate `demoted` line.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. `display::plan` prints `report.notes` as `note        ...` lines (display.rs:604) and the drain report prints its notes too (display.rs:718), so one mechanism explains the order change in both `athena plan` and `drain`, with exactly one line per demotion. A second mechanism in `display::plan` would print each demotion twice. `note_once` also keeps a re-plan within one drain run from repeating the line.

rejected.option: Both a note and a `demoted` line in display::plan
rejected.why: Duplicate lines in `athena plan`, which would break the 'one line per demoted item' criterion.
`drain` output would not explain the order change.

decisions.choice: `athena focus` fails before writing anything when git user.name is unset or blank. `Athena::set_focus` reads it with `self.git.config_get("user.name")` (athena-git lib.rs:586), trims it, and on none or blank bails with: `git user.name is not set; run git config user.name "Your Name" and try again`. It also rejects blank focus text with a clear message before the check.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. Without it the user would see an unclear record-validation error for an empty set_by. It follows set_priority, which checks its input before committing.

rejected.option: Fall back to a placeholder name such as 'unknown'
rejected.why: Writes a false author into a record.

decisions.choice: The focus record is `FocusRecord { n, at, text, set_by }` with deny_unknown_fields, path `records/focus/focus-<n>.json`, schema `athena.focus/1`. `Records` gets `focus: Vec<FocusRecord>` filled by an explicit arm in `Records::load` before the job-owned fallback arm. The latest is the highest n. `athena focus` with no text prints the current focus.
decisions.reason: A counter makes 'latest' unambiguous (as PriorityRecord.n does), and the explicit arm avoids the fallback's expect that every record names a job.

rejected.why: Two records in one second tie.
The brief puts it in AnyRecord.

decisions.choice: Config is `priority_caps: Option<PriorityCaps>` with skip_serializing_if is_none, reset in `reading_inputs`, read through `Config::priority_caps()` which falls back to 3 and 10. Validation rejects a cap of 0.
decisions.reason: Same pattern as the disk and drain tables. Existing reading digests stay byte-identical, and a config without the table still gets 3 and 10.

rejected.option: A non-Option struct with serde defaults
rejected.why: It would serialize into `reading_inputs` and change every existing reading digest.

decisions.choice: `Steps::priority_caps` (default: unlimited) and `Steps::person_set` (default: empty) are default trait methods. Only `RealSteps` overrides them, from `JobConfig::at(..).config.priority_caps()` and from `Records` priority records.
decisions.reason: The fake Steps in tests/drain.rs are not deliverables and must keep compiling and keep their plan order.

rejected.why: They would break the fakes in tests/drain.rs.

decisions.choice: Do not change the refusal corpus.
decisions.reason: The caps are not a refusal or matching rule. They reorder items and never refuse one. `Plan::refused` and `missing()` are untouched. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is run only as a regression check, and I cite no case ids because I added no input forms.

rejected.why: There is no new refusal or matching input form.

High pass: person-set items count first, then items demoted from urgent (never demoted again), then native high items in plan order; excess native high items drop to normal. Rebuild from the capped clones, set `demoted`, and return the capped entries. Leave `build` and `build_with` unchanged. risks.risk: `AnyRecord::Focus` could panic in `Records::load`, whose fallback arm expects every other record to name a job.
risks.mitigation: Add an explicit Focus arm before the fallback and test loading a repo that holds a focus record (step 4).

risks.risk: Adding fields to `Plan` and `StatusView` breaks struct literals in tests the plan cannot edit.
risks.mitigation: A grep found no `Plan {` or `StatusView {` literals outside plan.rs and status.rs. The producer fixes the plan.rs test literals with `..Default::default()` and marks `Plan.demoted` skip_serializing_if is_empty; `cargo test --locked` confirms.

risks.risk: Capping changes `drain` order in existing tests that use many urgent or high items.
risks.mitigation: The `Steps` default is unlimited, so fakes are unaffected. Only `RealSteps` applies 3 and 10, and the full suite runs in criterion 8.

risks.risk: The new config table changes the digest of existing readings.
risks.mitigation: Use an Option field skipped when none and reset in `reading_inputs`. Add a test that `reading_inputs()` equals that of the stripped config.

risks.risk: A demoted urgent item landing behind an equal-tier item triggers a false priority-contradiction note.
risks.mitigation: `build_capped` returns the capped entries and `Drain::prepare` passes them to `priority_violations`; the prepare test in step 8 covers it.

risks.risk: Person-set items alone could exceed a cap, leaving the tier larger than the cap.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended result of the rule that a person's record wins. The cap+1 unit test pins it, and the CHANGELOG entry says so.

risks.risk: Editing athena.toml trips the gate that requires the schema in the same job.
risks.mitigation: config.rs is a deliverable and holds the schema change.

risks.risk: Two focus calls racing could write the same n.
risks.mitigation: `commit_records` writes through git, so a duplicate path is refused. `set_focus` takes n from records at HEAD, as `set_priority` does, so the exposure is the same.

demonstrations.method: Three tests. (a) A unit test in plan.rs `mod tests` calls `Plan::build_capped` on five urgent entries (existing `entry` and `with_priority` helpers) with caps {urgent:3, high:10} and one person-set id. (b) A unit test in plan.rs with cap+1 person-set urgent entries asserts none is in `plan.demoted`. (c) An integration test in focus.rs queues 5 urgent requests with acceptance bullets, sets a priority record on one of them via `Athena::set_priority`, and calls `drain::plan` with `RealSteps::live`. It renders `display::plan` on the report. A fourth test in drain.rs `mod tests` runs `Drain::prepare` with a Steps double that returns caps {urgent:3} on 5 urgent entries plus one older native high entry, and asserts no note contains `contradicts priority`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core plan:: && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test focus && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli drain::
demonstrations.observes: Exactly 3 urgent ids come first in `plan.order`, the person-set id among them, and `plan.demoted` has 2 entries (urgent to high) whose ids come after the first 3. The rendered plan text has exactly 2 lines starting `note        demoted`, one per demoted id. With cap+1 person-set items, `demoted` has none of them. The prepare test has no 'contradicts priority' note, which proves violations are judged against the capped entries.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no capping all 5 stay urgent, `demoted` is empty and no demotion note is printed. If the person-set item were ranked by plan order it could be demoted. If `priority_violations` still ran on the uncapped entries, the prepare test would see a false contradiction note.

The unit tests pass plain entries, so there is no double. The integration test uses the real `RealSteps` over the Fixture with fake agents (`athena_agent::fake::deterministic_turn`, as drain.rs tests do), and real priority records from `Athena::set_priority` (exists, reading.rs:915). The `Steps` default methods and the `RealSteps` overrides are added in step 8.

open_questions: 'Person-set items first, most recent first' is read as keep-first, with person-set items never demoted. Recency then has no effect, so `person_set` is unordered. If the user wanted person-set items to be the first ones demoted, criterion 3 could not hold.

Whether `common` already offers a `RealSteps::live` helper or only tests/drain.rs does was not checked. If it is only in drain.rs, focus.rs builds `RealSteps::live` itself with a recording Lander, as drain.rs does.

Whether another test pins the exact list of athena.toml sections or Config keys (for example a docs or policy test in xtask) was not checked. `cargo test --locked` will show it; extend that test if it fails.
How the `common` fixture builds its athena.toml was not read. If it is a stripped copy, `priority_caps()` falls back to 3 and 10, which the criteria need.
Dependency raising is applied after capping, using each entry's own tier, so a prerequisite of an urgent item can still run early without counting against the cap. The brief does not address this.
Whether `Git::config_get` returns None or Some("") for an empty user.name was not read. `set_focus` trims and treats both as unset.
